t2.thesis: NIKE goes into this print already washed out - down 47% in twelve months, 51% below its 52-week high, on a consensus bar that has been walked down to $0.44 - so the consumer-cluster base rate broadly holds, but its own 10-K warning that Greater China and Converse drag all through fiscal 2027, and an incoming CFO's first call, pull it back to barely better than a coin flip.
reasons: Outside view first: the history study's buy-everything hit rate is 0.555 for the consumer cluster (n=436) and 0.538 for AMC reporters, so the honest starting point is about 0.55, not 0.50, and the entry open is a full session before an after-close print - the part of the window where the announcement premium sits.

The bar is low and has already been cut: consensus is $0.437 against $0.49 a year ago (-10.8%), walked down 2.6% over 90 days (D_eps_revision_90d_LR19), and NIKE beat consensus in each of the last four quarters (+81%, +41%, +24%, +466% vendor surprise).

This is a washed-out name, not a glamour one, so the LR20 growth-torpedo risk is largely spent: A_ret_12m_LR01 -47.3%, A_dist_from_52w_high -50.8%, forward P/E 16.5, P/S 1.13. Option positioning is mildly call-side on all three B-family signs - put/call volume 0.82, put/call OI 0.77, ATM call IV 0.78 vol points above the ATM put (LR12 +), and the 90%-strike put trades 3.8 vol points BELOW the ATM call, the opposite of the steep bearish smirk LR13 penalises. The literature review flags B-family priors as weak in today's retail-dominated weekly market, so this is a light thumb on the scale.

Against that, the downside is concrete and company-stated: the FY2026 10-K (filed 2026-07-15) says 'We expect negative impacts from Greater China and Converse to continue throughout fiscal 2027', and Q4's headline $0.72 EPS contained $0.52 of one-off IEEPA tariff recovery ($986m booked in cost of sales), so the underlying run-rate is far weaker than the print implied. Two of the last four reactions on this exact entry-open-to-exit-A-open window were -10.3%.

Name-specific left tail this window cannot hedge: David Denton became CFO on 2026-08-17 and delivers his first NIKE call, while the Chief Accounting Officer resigned effective 2026-09-04. An incoming CFO has the standard incentive to reset expectations; high analyst dispersion (0.275) and 9.0% short interest are the Berkman/Miller disagreement setup that LR08 scores negative.
t2.deciding_variable: The forward commentary on Greater China and the fiscal-2027 revenue and gross-margin trajectory given by the incoming CFO on the call - not the EPS surprise, which NIKE has beaten four quarters running while the stock still fell 10% twice.
